$comment: Standby target registry for the x10 database mesh (see docs/redundancy.md). METADATA ONLY — never put a URL, key, or password in this file; those live in environment variables / GitHub Actions secrets named after each target's envPrefix (<PREFIX>_URL, <PREFIX>_ANON_KEY, <PREFIX>_SERVICE_KEY, <PREFIX>_DB_URL; the _SUPABASE_URL/_DATABASE_URL spellings also work). Max 9 targets: primary + 9 = 10 databases. VERIFIED free-tier reality (Oct 2026): 2 ACTIVE Supabase projects per ACCOUNT (member), not per org — paused projects don't count. Warm (synchronized) standbys therefore need accounts: Jesse's account holds the primary + standby-1; Cooper's account holds standby-2 + standby-3. That is the $0 warm ceiling: 4 live copies. The rest are cold-archive rotation or future accounts.

targets.notes: First warm standby — Jesse's account, 2nd active project. Hourly sync, first failover choice. Different region from the primary (Canada Central) so one regional incident can't take both.
Second warm standby — Cooper's account, 1st active project. Account-level isolation: an account action against one account can't freeze both. Hourly sync via the same fan-out.
Third warm standby — Cooper's account, 2nd active project. Third region for region-dispersal.
Cold archive: paused project costs no active-project quota while paused. Re-seeded weekly by the sync workflow in seed mode. Revive = manual unpause + resync from the primary.
Reserved: 4th warm standby if a third account ever joins the fleet.
Reserved: 5th warm standby if a third account ever joins the fleet.
Reserved: 7th warm standby (fourth account). Primary + these nine slots = ten databases total.
